title: Company research API: research a company by name or website
summary: How to research companies with an API: send a name or website, and Sixtyfour returns your fields, the pages it read and, on request, a score for each field.
body_markdown:
A company research API takes what you know about a company, such as its name or website, researches it when you ask and returns the fields you define, with the sources they came from. A lookup against a stored company database returns the record a provider already holds instead. Research suits fields specific to your workflow, small or new companies, and facts someone needs to check at the source.


A company information API usually looks a company up in a stored database and returns the record it holds, which is quick and consistent in shape for standard fields at volume. A company research API does the work when you ask, reading sources across the web and returning the fields you define with the pages they came from. Many teams use a lookup for standard firmographics and research for questions a record does not answer, such as who owns a company or what it announced this year.


Yes. Sixtyfour's Company Intelligence endpoint takes a company name, website, domain or LinkedIn page and returns the fields you describe in a struct, with the pages they were read on and, if you ask, a 0 to 100 confidence score and a justification for each field. Its People Intelligence endpoint does the same for a person, and both have sync, async and bulk versions. Anything the research could not establish comes back empty for a person on your team to decide.


With Sixtyfour, upload the list as one Bulk Intelligence job to the company endpoint: a CSV, JSON, JSONL or NDJSON file of up to 100 MB and 100,000 rows, plus a config that names the fields and the tier. The submission returns a task ID and a credit estimate, job status reports progress while it runs, and a completed job carries signed links to the result files or calls your webhook. An Idempotency-Key header makes the submission safe to retry.


A Sixtyfour Company Intelligence run takes up to 10 minutes, so a synchronous call needs a client timeout of at least 15 minutes. In production, start the job at the async endpoint, which returns a task ID at once, and poll job status every 10 seconds or slower, or pass a webhook URL to receive the result when the job completes. A sync call that times out keeps running and is charged, and Company Intelligence has no retry key, so store the task ID and never start the same company twice by accident.


Ask for field confidence. Each field then comes back with a 0 to 100 score, a short justification and the URLs it was read on, and the named levels run from Confirmed at 85 and above to Unreliable below 15. Send anything under your threshold, anything with no sources and any empty field to a person, who can start from the pages the research found.


As of November 2026, Company Intelligence costs 0.3 credits a company at the micro tier, 1 at low (the default), 5 at medium and 15 at high, which is enabled on request. Field confidence, finding people at the company and the org chart cost nothing extra, a failed single-company job is not charged, and bulk jobs cost the same per row. Filter Search, for building the list, costs 0.1 credits per result returned.
